title: Store the SMTP relay password in the environment's Key Vault
purpose: Put the SMTP relay password of a PIM Manager environment into its Key Vault, and let the environment's managed identities read that one secret.
whenToRun: When PIM Manager sends mail through an SMTP relay (Settings > Mail & alerting, or Get Started > Mail sender > SMTP relay) and could not write the password itself, or when the relay password changes. Not needed for the shared-mailbox mode.

runAs.name: Key Vault Secrets Officer
runAs.why: Writes the secret. When you can manage the vault's access (User Access Administrator or Owner) but not its secrets, the script grants you this role on that one vault and retries.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: the environment's Key Vault (Owner or Role Based Access Control Administrator work too)
runAs.why: Gives each sending identity read access on the one secret, and, when needed, gives you Key Vault Secrets Officer on the vault.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.why: Finds the vault by name in the subscription.

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.why: Creates the Key Vault when it does not exist.

runAs.name: browser sign-in to Azure (first-party public client 'Microsoft Azure PowerShell'), or the Invardia Support app (-AdminAppId + -AdminSecret)
runAs.scope: Azure Resource Manager and Key Vault in your tenant
runAs.why: No PowerShell module and no certificate. The Support app's secret is accepted only for Invardia support; a person signs in in the browser.

changes.object: Key Vault -VaultName (Azure RBAC authorisation, standard SKU, soft delete 90 days, the resource group's region) -- only with -CreateVault and only when it does not exist
changes.why: The relay password must live in the environment's own vault, never in SQL, the page or a log.
changes.undo: Delete the Key Vault (it stays soft-deleted for 90 days; purge it to remove it at once).

changes.object: secret -SecretName (default PIM-SmtpRelayPassword) holding the SMTP relay password, content type 'PIM Manager SMTP relay password'; a new version when it exists. The value is read back to compare and never printed.
changes.why: PIM Manager reads the password at send time with its managed identities.
changes.undo: Delete the secret (Key Vault > Secrets), or set the previous version back.

changes.object: Azure role assignment for the account running the script (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments) -- ONLY when Key Vault refuses the secret write
changes.why: Someone who manages the vault's access but not its secrets can then write the secret without a second person.
changes.undo: Key Vault > Access control (IAM) > remove your 'Key Vault Secrets Officer' assignment.

changes.object: Azure role assignment for each -ManagedIdentityObjectId (the Manager's and the engine job's identities), with a fixed name so a re-run does not create a second one
changes.scope: the one secret only (<vault>/secrets/<secret name>), never the whole vault
changes.why: The sending identities must read the password at send time, and nothing else in the vault.
changes.undo: Key Vault > the secret > Access control (IAM) > remove the assignment.

changes.object: the result file -OutFile (JSON: vault, secret name, what was created and granted; never the password) -- only when -OutFile is given and not under -WhatIf
changes.why: For automation that reads the outcome.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: Your tenant id; a sign-in in another tenant is refused.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription that holds the environment's Key Vault.

parameters.name: ManagedIdentityObjectId
parameters.help: Object ids of the identities that send (the Manager's and the engine job's); each gets read access on the secret only.

parameters.name: Password
parameters.help: The relay password as a SecureString. Never type it as plain text on the command line.

parameters.name: CreateVault
parameters.help: Create the vault when it does not exist (needs -ResourceGroup).

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Invardia support only: the Invardia Support app's application id (with -AdminSecret) instead of the browser sign-in.

parameters.name: AdminSecret
parameters.help: Invardia support only: the Invardia Support app's secret.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the result (no password) as JSON to this file.

readsOnly: the Key Vaults of the subscription (to find -VaultName), and the vault's authorisation model
the secret, right after writing it, to compare it (never printed)
network: localhost (the browser returns the sign-in to a local port on this computer)
whatIf: Signs in, finds the vault, asks for no password, and prints one "What if:" line per change: create the vault (with -CreateVault), write the secret, the Key Vault Secrets Officer grant to you (only if the write would be refused), and Key Vault Secrets User on the secret for each managed identity. Nothing is written, no -OutFile either.
undo: Remove the 'Key Vault Secrets User' assignments on the secret and any 'Key Vault Secrets Officer' assignment the script gave you on the vault, delete the secret, and delete the vault if the script created it.
